suggestions.title: Paths of Glory
suggestions.description: Your war shelf is Saving Private Ryan, Das Boot, Apocalypse Now, Downfall, Schindler's List and The Pianist — all of them about men surviving a war. This one is about a war surviving men, and it is the shortest and coldest film Kubrick ever made. He directed and co-wrote it at 28, adapting Humphrey Cobb's 1935 novel, which was itself built on the real Souain corporals affair of 1915 — French soldiers shot by their own army as an example. Kirk Douglas is Colonel Dax, a criminal lawyer in peacetime, who leads a suicidal attack on the Ant Hill because General Mireau (George Macready) wants a promotion and General Broulard (Adolphe Menjou) wants the paperwork to look clean; when the assault fails, three men are chosen by lot and court-martialled for cowardice, and Dax has to defend them in a trial whose verdict was written before it began. Around them: Ralph Meeker, Wayne Morris, Timothy Carey, Joe Turkel, and — in the tavern scene, the only woman in the whole film — Christiane Harlan, whom Kubrick married the following year and stayed with until he died. The screenplay is by Kubrick, Calder Willingham and the pulp novelist Jim Thompson. Shot black and white in Bavaria on a small budget, released in October 1957 at 88 minutes, it was banned in France until 1975 for its portrait of the French high command, and it is the reason the anti-war film has a template: the machine does not care who is in it. IMDb 8.4.

suggestions.title: Taxi Driver
suggestions.description: Every crime film on this shelf so far is a professional's story — Goodfellas, The Departed, Heat, The Usual Suspects, The Godfather. This is the amateur's, and it is the one the whole shelf is standing on. Martin Scorsese directed from an original screenplay by Paul Schrader, written in a few weeks while Schrader was living in his car and drinking himself into a hole in Los Angeles, with Travis Bickle as the version of himself he was afraid of becoming. Robert De Niro got an actual New York taxi licence and worked twelve-hour night shifts in the cab before shooting. The score is Bernard Herrmann's last — he recorded it in December 1975 and died the night after the final session, so the film opens with a dead man's music announcing the end of an era. Around De Niro: Jodie Foster at twelve as Iris, Cybill Shepherd as Betsy, Harvey Keitel as Sport, Albert Brooks as Tom, Peter Boyle as the Wizard, and Scorsese himself in the back seat of the cab describing what he wants to do to his wife. It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1976 and was nominated for four Academy Awards including Best Picture, winning none; 'You talkin' to me?' is De Niro's and not in the script; the ending is a hallucination or a mercy, and the film refuses to say which. It was read as a provocation, then as a diagnosis, and now sits high on every list of the best American films ever made. IMDb 8.2.

suggestions.title: Oppenheimer
suggestions.description: The newest thing in the database and the one with the most to say to what you actually spend your days on: the sovereign stack question, told as a horror film about a man who builds the thing and then spends the rest of his life in rooms full of people deciding what he is allowed to be. Christopher Nolan wrote and directed it, adapting Kai Bird and Martin J. Sherwin's Pulitzer-winning biography American Prometheus, and resisted the obvious movies at every turn: no CGI for the Trinity test, an hour of black-and-white for the 1954 security hearing, three timelines cut against each other across 180 minutes, shot by Hoyte van Hoytema on large-format 65mm and IMAX film. Cillian Murphy carries it as J. Robert Oppenheimer, with Emily Blunt as Kitty, Matt Damon as General Leslie Groves, Robert Downey Jr. as Lewis Strauss — the performance that finally stopped him being Tony Stark — Florence Pugh as Jean Tatlock, and Kenneth Branagh, Josh Hartnett, Rami Malek, Jason Clarke, Tom Conti and Gary Oldman filling the rest of the century. Ludwig Göransson wrote the score, and ten of the eleven had to be defeated by the eleventh. Released 21 July 2023 into the Barbenheimer weekend, it grossed close to a billion dollars to become the highest-grossing biopic ever made, and won seven Academy Awards including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. IMDb 8.2.
